assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: incapable
driver_capability: gap:interrupt
=> route: frozen

## agent — yes

Hermes' default subcommand is the interactive REPL: `hermes_cli/main.py:14766` defaults `args.command` to `"chat"`, and `chat` is one of `_AGENT_COMMANDS` (`main.py:14588`). That REPL is a prompt_toolkit full-screen TUI — `cli.py:60-62` imports prompt_toolkit, `cli.py:14766` builds the `TextArea` input area, `cli.py:13841` creates the `KeyBindings` set, and `cli.py:14326-14327` binds `@kb.add('c-c') def handle_ctrl_c` whose docstring ladder is "1. Cancel active sudo/approval/clarify prompt / 2. Interrupt the running agent (first press) / 3. Force exit" (the live interrupt banner is at `cli.py:14403`). So keystrokes injected into the controlling terminal are indistinguishable from typing, and Ctrl-C is a real interrupt — exactly the mechanism this scenario needs on the agent side. Verified against the installed Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20).

## daemon — incapable (today)

Two independent blockers; only the second is architecture, and the metadata says so loudly so the cheap fix is not mis-routed.

**Blocker 1 — irrlicht has no control write path to a hermes session at all (product).** `core/adapters/inbound/agents/hermes/agent.go` `Agent()` leaves `Control` at its zero value (the doc comment says so deliberately: "nothing in this PR exercised that") and declares exactly one permission, `store` (KindObserve). The operative consequence is not the zero `SupportsInput` — that field currently has NO runtime consumer anywhere in the repo (a grep for `SupportsInput`/`supports_input` across `core/`, `platforms/` and the macOS app finds only the seven adapter declarations and the domain definition in `core/domain/agent/declaration.go`; it is declarative today). The operative gate is the missing permission: `InputService.resolve` (`core/application/services/input_service.go`) runs betaOn → `consent.Granted(state.Adapter, "control")` → `controller.Controllable`, and `PermissionService.Granted` (`permission_service.go`) is `s.set.Get(agentName, key) == StateGranted` for a key no adapter declares. `Start()` under `IRRLICHT_PERMISSION_MODE=grant-all` iterates `a.Permissions` and so grants only DECLARED keys; `Answer()` rejects an undeclared pair with `ErrUnknownPermission`; `Snapshot()` only lists declared permissions, so the wizard never even offers the grant. Net: `InputService.Controllable` is false for every hermes session, `annotateControllable` (`core/cmd/irrlichd/handlers.go:120-130`) stamps `controllable:false` on every hermes row so the dashboard offers no affordance, and `SendInput`/`SendCommand`/`Interrupt` all return `ErrControlDisabled` (403) — locally and, identically, through the relay forwarder, which passes the same gate. The scenario's first acceptance criterion ("reports controllable once the backchannel toggle is on and 'control' is granted") therefore cannot be satisfied: there is nothing to grant.

The terminal-backend half, by contrast, is already fine and adapter-agnostic: `PIDManager.captureLauncher` (`core/application/services/pid_manager.go:277-289`) stamps a `Launcher` from the process env for any PID-bound session, and `Controller.Controllable` (`core/adapters/outbound/control/controller.go:118`) only asks `resolveBackend(state.Launcher) != backendNone`. A `hermes chat` running in a tmux pane already resolves a scriptable backend — so blocker 1 really is a ~6-line adapter change plus the `contracttesting.AssertPermissionGated` obligation the repo requires for a new modify-kind permission, not architecture. This is the exact shape mistral-vibe carried before commit 5e22e47 flipped it to daemon=full.

**Blocker 2 — the interrupt criterion is unobservable on this transport, whatever the adapter declares (architecture).** Acceptance criterion 3 asserts "an interrupt cancels an in-flight turn; the session settles back to ready". The sibling cell `replaydata/agents/hermes/scenarios/2-20_user-esc-interrupt` establishes, from the Hermes source plus the live store schema, that an interrupted hermes turn persists NO terminal row: `finish_reason` is never `stop` on the interrupt paths, `_turn_exit_reason` is an in-memory diagnostic, and there is no turns table. `Watcher.turnIsDone` (`hermes/watcher.go`) returns true only for `role='assistant' AND finish_reason='stop'`, so the post-interrupt settle never fires and the session sticks in `working`. Declaring `Control{Interrupt: InterruptCtrlC}` would let the daemon SEND the Ctrl-C; it would not let it SEE the result. Clearing that needs the on_session_end hook tier described in 2-20, not an adapter declaration.

**Why `incapable` and not `bug`.** `bug` means a trace exists that the daemon mis-handles, and it routes to record-known-failing — i.e. record now. Recording this cell today would be actively misleading in two ways. First, the row's recorded specs (claudecode, mistral-vibe) assert only `session_birth → injected_turn(working) → settle(ready)`, and the drivers produce that arc with their own `tmux send-keys` (`mistral-vibe/driver-interactive.sh` `step_interrupt`/`type_enter`) — they never call InputService — so every phase would pass and the verify engine would report `known_failing_now_passing` while irrlicht cannot in fact control a hermes session. Second, the spec vocabulary has no way to assert the thing that is actually broken: `internal/validate/expected.go` phases carry `expected_state`/`new_session`/`same_session_as` only — there is no `controllable` assertion. With no trace to mis-handle (blocker 1 leaves no control path in existence) and a transport limit no declaration can clear (blocker 2), `incapable` + `frozen` is the honest routing: do not record, document the unfreeze.

## driver — gap:interrupt

`replaydata/agents/hermes/driver-interactive.sh:113` declares `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"`, and the dispatch at `:300-301` maps `interrupt` and `keys` to `not_implemented`. This scenario's process step 3 ("an interrupt delivers Ctrl-C") needs the `interrupt` step, so the driver is `gap:interrupt` — the same gap this agent already carries on 2-20. It is tooling work, not an observability limit. The port is NOT a copy of the reference step: `claudecode`/`aider` `step_interrupt` sends `Escape`, which is not bound to interrupt in Hermes; the hermes port must send `C-c` ONCE (a second press within 2s force-exits the REPL), i.e. the mistral-vibe `step_interrupt` shape (`tmux send-keys -t "$SESSION" C-c`).

## Surfaces that could carry control later (unlock path, NOT the verdict)

Hermes has two programmatic input surfaces beyond keystroke injection, neither wired to irrlicht: `hermes acp` (an ACP JSON-RPC agent server over stdio — `acp_adapter/entry.py`, `acp_adapter/server.py`) and the TUI's websocket gateway (`tui_gateway/server.py`, `tui_gateway/entry.py`, whose `update_session_cwd` callers are already why `sessions.cwd` is TUI-only per `hermes/adapter.go`). Either could deliver input without a terminal backend. Note that `acp` is in the adapter's `serviceSubcommands` exclusion list (`hermes/adapter.go`), so an ACP-based control path would also require revisiting that exclusion. Both are speculative future work and neither changes today's verdict.

## What is NOT proven

No daemon was run and no session was driven (this verb spends no agent-CLI tokens and runs no recording). Everything above is source-level: the irrlicht gate chain read end-to-end, the Hermes REPL key bindings read in the installed v0.19.0 tree, and the interrupt-observability claim inherited from the sibling 2-20 cell's evidence rather than re-derived.
caveats: Labeling tension, stated openly: blocker 1 (no Control axis, no ControlPermission) is the same shape mistral-vibe's cell records as a former `daemon=bug`. This cell calls it `incapable` because of the ROUTE it implies, not because the fix is hard — recording today would drive tmux send-keys, satisfy every phase in the row's spec shape, and report `known_failing_now_passing` while irrlicht still cannot control hermes. If the matrix later gains a way to assert `controllable` in a spec, this cell should be re-judged as bug/record-known-failing.

Blocker 2 is inherited, not re-derived here: the claim that an interrupted hermes turn writes no terminal row comes from the sibling cell 2-20_user-esc-interrupt (source + live-store evidence), which itself flags that no live Ctrl-C was ever driven. If that turns out wrong, criterion 3 becomes observable and only blocker 1 remains.

The relay half of the scenario (criterion 5) was not separately analyzed: the relay forwarder reaches the same InputService gate, so it is blocked by blocker 1 identically — but the relay-token/workspace scoping was not read for this cell.

Only the injection half of the scenario would be unfrozen by the product fix. Declaring Control + ControlPermission makes the recordable arc (ready → working → ready on injected text) real and would justify re-assessing to yes/full plus a driver-gap port; criterion 3 still needs the hook tier.

`Control.SupportsInput` has no runtime consumer today, so a future fix that sets it WITHOUT adding agent.ControlPermission() would change nothing — the permission is the gate. Anyone acting on the unfreeze must add both.

sources.note: Agent(): Control left at its zero value by design (the doc comment says SupportsInput was never exercised in the onboarding PR), and Permissions carries ONLY PermissionKeyStore (KindObserve) — no agent.ControlPermission().

resolve(): betaOn → consent.Granted(state.Adapter, ControlPermissionKey="control") → controller.Controllable. The consent step is what hermes fails; SendInput/SendCommand/Interrupt/Controllable all route through it, so all return ErrControlDisabled for hermes.

Granted() = set.Get(agent,key)==StateGranted; Start() grants only DECLARED permissions even under IRRLICHT_PERMISSION_MODE=grant-all (it loops a.Permissions); Answer() returns ErrUnknownPermission for an undeclared pair; Snapshot() lists only declared permissions. So "control" for hermes is ungrantable and unofferable.

annotateControllable walks the group tree and stamps session.AgentGroup.Controllable from the InputService gate — false for every hermes row, so the dashboard never offers the input affordance (session.Controllable is the json `controllable` field, core/domain/session/grouped.go:37-41).

Controller.Controllable is adapter-agnostic: resolveBackend(state.Launcher) != backendNone. Together with PIDManager.captureLauncher (pid_manager.go:277-289) this means a `hermes chat` in a tmux pane ALREADY has a scriptable backend — the backend half is not the blocker.

Control axis (SupportsInput/Interrupt/Presets, zero value = not controllable) + ControlPermission() (KindModify, key "control"). A repo-wide grep for SupportsInput/supports_input finds only the seven adapter declarations and this file — the field has no runtime consumer, so the declared permission is the operative gate.

Precedent for this exact shape: vibe's cell records that the PRIOR verdict was daemon=bug "because agent.go declared NO Control (zero value -> SupportsInput=false)", and commit 5e22e47 (Control{SupportsInput,Interrupt:InterruptCtrlC,Presets} + ControlPermission() + TestAgent_Control_Backchannel) flipped it to daemon=full. That is the template for the hermes unfreeze.

step_interrupt is `tmux send-keys -t "$SESSION" C-c` — the driver MIRRORS the backchannel keystroke rather than calling the daemon's control API. Hence a recording of this row exercises the observation arc only, which is why a known-failing recording here would look green.
DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"; the `interrupt)` and `keys)` dispatch arms call not_implemented. The scenario needs an interrupt step -> driver=gap:interrupt.

Blocker 2's evidence base: an interrupted hermes turn persists no terminal row (finish_reason never 'stop', turn_exit_reason in-memory only, no turns table), so Watcher.turnIsDone stays false and the post-interrupt settle is unobservable — daemon=incapable on that row, with the on_session_end hook tier (turn_finalizer.py:668-684) named as the unlock.

The spec phase vocabulary is phase/expected_state/new_session/same_session_as/relative_to — there is no `controllable` assertion, so the thing that is actually broken for hermes cannot be expressed as a known_failing phase.

Hermes v0.19.0 REPL: prompt_toolkit imports, KeyBindings(), TextArea input area, and @kb.add('c-c') handle_ctrl_c whose ladder interrupts the running agent on the first press (banner "Interrupting agent... (press Ctrl+C again to force exit)"). Confirms agent=yes and that the interrupt key is C-c, not Escape.
_AGENT_COMMANDS = {None, "chat", "acp", "rl"} and args.command defaults to "chat" — the bare `hermes` invocation IS the interactive REPL this scenario would drive.

UNLOCK PATH ONLY (not the verdict): `hermes acp` runs an ACP JSON-RPC agent server over stdio — a programmatic input surface. Note `acp` is in hermes/adapter.go's serviceSubcommands exclusion list, so an ACP-based control path also needs that exclusion revisited.

UNLOCK PATH ONLY (not the verdict): the TUI's websocket gateway (dispatch/write_json), already relevant to this adapter as the sole writer of sessions.cwd. A second candidate control surface that needs no terminal backend.

preconditions: FROZEN — not recordable today, and a recording would be a FALSE GREEN. irrlicht has no control write path to a hermes session: hermes/agent.go declares neither Control nor agent.ControlPermission(), so InputService's consent gate refuses every SendInput/Interrupt and every hermes row is annotated controllable:false. The row's drivers inject with their own `tmux send-keys`, never through InputService, so the recorded phases would pass while the capability under test does not exist.

UNFREEZE (daemon, product — cheap): in core/adapters/inbound/agents/hermes/agent.go declare Control{SupportsInput: true, Interrupt: agent.InterruptCtrlC} AND append agent.ControlPermission() to Permissions (the permission is the operative gate; SupportsInput alone changes nothing). Wire contracttesting.AssertPermissionGated for the new modify-kind permission per AGENTS.md, and add a TestAgent_Control_Backchannel-style assertion mirroring core/adapters/inbound/agents/vibe/adapter_test.go. That alone makes the injection half recordable in the shape claudecode/mistral-vibe use (ready -> working -> ready on injected text).

UNFREEZE (daemon, architecture): the scenario's interrupt criterion ("an interrupt cancels an in-flight turn; the session settles back to ready") stays unobservable after that fix — an interrupted hermes turn writes no terminal row (sibling cell 2-20). It needs the on_session_end hook tier (agent/turn_finalizer.py:668-684 fires per TURN carrying interrupted/completed), whose hook endpoint must follow the resolved bind addr, not :7837 (contracttesting.AssertHookEndpointFollowsBindAddr, #1178).

UNFREEZE (driver): port an `interrupt` step into replaydata/agents/hermes/driver-interactive.sh (currently not_implemented at :300) and add `interrupt` to DRIVE_ELICITS at :113. It must `tmux send-keys C-c` ONCE — Escape (what claudecode/aider step_interrupt sends) is not bound to interrupt in Hermes, and a second C-c within 2s force-exits the REPL.

Recording prereqs once unfrozen: the backchannel beta toggle ON and the hermes `control` consent granted (in addition to `store`); the agent launched inside a scriptable backend (tmux pane) so a Launcher resolves; HERMES_HOME exported identically to driver and daemon; sqlite3 on PATH for wait_turn; exactly one live interactive hermes process (source='cli' rows carry no cwd).
